doc.title: Ashley Keating and Allan Whitworth Interview, 1963-03-22

title: Australian jazz conventions and their traditional social events
summary: Keating explains the committee that runs the annual convention and describes the rorty old do, jazz and a jug, and the how-you've-been-keeping night, with talk of drinking.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: What is, uh, kind of, uh, committee is this? Explain it exactly. I don't get that.

Well, uh, as the things, uh, an annual, uh, convention, the jazz convention is an annual convention. Of course, it's like, uh, any other committee. They have a president, a secretary, a treasurer, uh, vice presidents, et cetera, uh, and it's placed in the hands of these men to see that, uh, a program is organized, halls are booked, uh, musicians in all states of Australia advised of, of the date and the, uh, locality of, of the convention, uh, and also to take care of such arrangements as, uh, billeting musicians and, uh, arranging social functions such as the picnic, the rorty old do, the jazz and a jug, um, and other,
uh,

functions which are traditional parts now of the, uh, conventions. There's been 17 of them and they occur every year from the 26th of December of that, of the year to the New Year's Day of the incoming year.
What is this, uh, functions that you're talking about? I can get the names of them.

Uh, uh, well, the rorty old do, uh, is, uh, an Australian term for a, a wild time, I'd say, and be the best way to put it. Uh, there's free beer, free food, uh, plenty of music, and, uh, a good time is had by all. Uh, uh, it's a traditional part of the, uh, conventions, there's been one every year, uh, the idea being to listen to the music while you're sober and, uh, then to make a complete mess of yourself once you become incoherent.
Ha, ha,
ha, ha, ha, And Australians alike then,
uh,
Yes, I'd say, even the non-jazz Australian, non-jazz loving Australian is a pretty hard doer as regards alcoholic beverages. Do you think transportation would help? Uh,
I,
I refrain from answering. Ha, ha, ha,
ha, ha, ha,
You wouldn't send them all to New Zealand? Uh, I don't think so. No. Well, how do you spell that rorty old do? Uh, R-O- T-Y. R-O- R-T-Y.
R-O-R-T-Y.

R-O-R-T-Y. I think so. It's, it's, it's, it's actually, it's an idiomatic term. I think it is R-O-R-T-Y-O-L-E-D-O. Uh, It's all one word? No, it's, it's three words. Three words. It's the rorty old do.
Then you said something about jazz and a jug.

Jazz and a jug, that's another excuse for getting drunk. Uh, that usually takes part at a, uh, an outer suburban hotel, uh, where the musicians are either transboarded by, uh, a riverboat. There's always a riverboat trip. And usually, uh, the riverboat trip, uh, terminates at some particular hotel where, uh, music is again played in the beer garden. And, uh, those who wish to destroy quite an amount of liquor can do so and listen to the music. And, uh, other traditional functions, uh, uh, usually on the first night of the convention also there's the how you've been keeping night where everyone, uh, makes, uh, renews their acquaintances from the previous year's convention. It's also another free, uh, grog night. Uh-huh.
I see.
